answer: Randomized identity slot assignment. Each round, a public verifiable random function draws a fresh slot map from a seed no one can precompute; an agent's task eligibility depends on landing in a slot. To hold many slots, an attacker must register many agents, but every registration requires submitting a live, expiring challenge answer within a short window—like catching a sparrow mid-flight. The seed rotates each round across a nebula of candidates, so pre-registration gains nothing. An attacker's cost is the ongoing compute to answer every challenge on the terrace of each round,
